hypothesis: A fault absent from the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue still leaves three independent expressions -- a break in slope, an elongated ridge or trough, and an edge in the potential fields -- and requiring several of them to corroborate the same cell locates it better than any one of them.
mechanism: 13 catalogue-free channels (DEM scarp curvature, multiscale local relief, multiscale Hessian ridge/valley, an 8-orientation matched line filter, and TMI / tilt-angle / isostatic-gravity gradients), each average-rank normalised inside the valid footprint and averaged (dem3 = dem_scarp_curvature + dem_local_relief_tpi3 + dem_direction_line), non-maximum-suppressed in a 3x3 window, top 90,000 cells, restricted to >= 300 m from the catalogue, emitted at value 1.0.
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Rough bedrock terrain. Every DEM channel is a form of local relief, and the USGS State Geologic Map Compilation draws most of its faults in ranges, so a detector that simply finds mountains will score well on the proxy instrument. The geophysical channels (TMI/gravity gradients) were included precisely because they do not have that confound, and they are the ones that scored worst on the proxy -- which is why the confound is stated rather than dismissed.

supervised_arm.instrument: hide-and-recover, 4 spatially blocked folds of 512 px blocks, 3 px collar, visible catalogue masked pixel-exactly

shipped_arm.instrument: credit per unit mass vs USGS SGMC off-catalogue faults, exact 300 m triangular kernel, src/gems62/metric.py
shipped_arm.class: MEASURED on a proxy truth set

submission_note: H63: 90k dots; rank-average corroboration of DEM scarp curvature, local relief and a directional line filter, >=300 m off the catalogue.
